Within the existing corridor of Lincoln Highway, several alternatives were available for consideration as discussed below.
A. Not to Improve This Highway Facility
The non-improvement of Lincoln Highway would not alleviate present traffic congestion nor would it avoid future congestion. It would not eliminate present accident producing conditions or avoid the increase in such accidents expected to accompany the increased traffic volume projected through the year 1990. At the present time this section of highway and its structures are deteriorating at a rapid and expensive rate. Failure to improve this section of Lincoln Highway would also increase air and noise pollution in the area due to the congestion caused by the anticipated increase in traffic volumes which the present roadway is incapable of handling. Lincoln Highway is a major East-West Highway, failure to improve it to accomodate the projected traffic requirements would reduce the cross-country and cross-state mobility of many residents of southern Cook County, the most populous county in the State of Illinois. It would also be detrimental to interstate travel between the heavily populated area of southern Cook County and industrial northwestern Indiana.
B. To Improve This Highway Facility
Consideration of the extensive residential and commercial developments, long established in the area through which this improvement will pass, has limited the location of the improvement to the present alignment. The design study for this project considered how to best accommodate the highway improvement largely within the existing right-of-way with limited land acquisition and limited disruption to business and neighborhood values, increasing safety and adding the traffic capacity required for the design year 1990.
Within the realm of constructing the improvement two alternates were studied.
